metadata.title: River Moves the Bank.
metadata.source: chapters/01-randomness-and-first-prompts.md § 'Inside one prediction step' (line 102) — the single sentence this reel expands

worked_example.disclosure: Every number in this reel is invented by the author for legibility. It is not measured from any model, and no published figure is reproduced. The chapter states the CLAIM (bank-after-river differs from bank-after-savings) and publishes no vectors, scores, or weights for it.
worked_example.label_rule: The stamp is persistent on every mechanism beat (B03–B07), not shown once and dropped. A viewer joining mid-scroll must see it.
simplifications_declared_on_screen: W_Q = W_K = W_V = I (identity) — real models learn these
one attention head (real models: many, in parallel)
one layer (real models: the block repeats many times)
no positional encoding, no residual add, no layer norm, no output projection
worked_example.arithmetic_verified_by: scratch script re-deriving every printed figure from the embeddings; weights printed to 3 d.p. sum to exactly 1.000 (2 d.p. would print 1.01 — that is why 3 d.p. is the on-screen format)
worked_example.mirror_symmetry_note: run_b is the exact mirror of run_a. That is a designed property of the chosen embeddings, not a finding — narration and the B07 card both say so.

boundary_claim.establishes: The SHAPE of one scaled dot-product attention operation: score every pair, normalize the scores into weights that sum to one, return a weighted sum of value vectors — and therefore that the same token's vector is context-dependent.
does_not_establish: that real learned W_Q / W_K / W_V behave like the identity matrices used here
how multi-head attention assigns different relations to different heads in parallel
what repeated layers do — how a token's representation changes as the block is stacked
that any real model's 'bank' axes correspond to interpretable directions like money or water
any quantitative claim at all: no number here is measured
boundary_claim.stated_verbatim_on_screen: What this single-head 2D example does not establish is how multi-head attention handles dozens of nuanced semantic dimensions simultaneously.
boundary_claim.stated_in: B09 (Ch1AttnMultiHead) — full-frame, and read aloud verbatim

beats.narration_text: Namaste — this is Tom, in for Bear. Chapter one says one sentence in passing: the vector for bank after river ends up somewhere different from the vector for bank after savings. One sentence. Let's open it.

shot.visual_intent: The Claude composer types the chapter's own sentence back at it as a question, and the ask lands answered — three output lines that are the episode's spine.

show.event: cream Claude app, serif greeting 'Namaste, Tom' above the composer
the ask types itself into the composer

props.command: Chapter 1 says the vector for `bank` after `river` ends up somewhere different from the vector for `bank` after `savings`. Show me the arithmetic that moves it.
props.runningText: reading chapter 1 — randomness and first prompts…
output: The chapter states it in one clause and moves on. It publishes no numbers for it.
The mechanism is scaled dot-product attention: score every pair, normalize, mix.
What follows is a constructed 2-D example — small enough to check by hand.

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. A word's vector is not looked up — it is recomputed. Context rewrites it. Same word, two sentences, two different vectors. That mechanism has a name: attention.

shot.visual_intent: The overview is written in front of the viewer. The writer first types the framing a viewer arrives with — a vector is 'looked up' — then deletes it and types 'recomputed'. That swap is exactly the misconception the body dismantles.

show.event: empty cream page, caret waiting through the 0.8s lead
line 1 types; 'looked up' lands in terracotta, marked for deletion
'looked up' is backspaced away and 'recomputed' types in its place
line 2 types
line 3 types; the corrected overview stands complete and holds

props.text:

beats.act: ACT I — the problem: one word, one row
beats.narration_text: Before attention, every token is just a row in a lookup table. Here are two sentences. The river bank. The savings bank. Both contain bank, and both pull the identical row. Same numbers. The table has no idea which bank you meant.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no embedding-table scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.

shot.visual_intent: The static embedding table as the thing that CANNOT tell the two sentences apart. Two sentence strips, one table, two identical arrows landing on the same highlighted row — the collision IS the beat.

show.event: the embedding table sets: four token rows, two numeric columns, axis headers greyed
two mono sentence strips slide in above the table — 'The river bank.' and 'The savings bank.'
the word `bank` underlines in both strips simultaneously
two arrows draw down from both strips and converge on the SAME table row; the row highlights terracotta — the ONE accent
the row's values (2, 2) enlarge and hold, duplicated beside each sentence to show they are byte-identical
a dashed 'CONTEXT' input port is drawn on the table and left visibly unconnected

props.row_order_note: The highlighted row is listed FIRST so the converging arrow lands on it without crossing the rows above. Row order in a lookup table is arbitrary; the arrow's legibility is not.

beats.narration_text: Now the honest part. Real attention runs in thousands of dimensions with learned matrices. Everything from here is a constructed two-dimensional example, built so you can check the arithmetic yourself. Axis one, money. Axis two, water. Bank sits exactly between them.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no 2-D vector-space scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.
beats.honesty_gate: This beat is where the CONSTRUCTED stamp is established. It persists on B04–B07.

shot.visual_intent: The constructed-example declaration is the SUBJECT of this beat, not a footnote on it. A left ledger names every simplification; a right plane places the four tokens. The terracotta stamp lands before any number is used for anything.

the terracotta CONSTRUCTED EXAMPLE stamp lands rotated over the ledger head — the ONE accent

beats.act: ACT II — step 1: query times key
beats.narration_text: Attention asks one question per token. Bank is the query; every token is a key; the score is their dot product. Bank with the, four. With river, six. With itself, eight. Then divide by the square root of the dimension — root two.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no dot-product worked-arithmetic scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.

shot.visual_intent: Three rows of worked arithmetic that a viewer can verify while watching. Each row shows the literal multiply-and-add, not a result asserted. The scaling column is drawn as a real step, not omitted.

show.event: the query chip `bank (2, 2)` sets top-left with the Q label; three key chips stack beneath it
column headers draw: q · k  |  ÷ √2  |  scaled
row 1 writes itself term by term — 2×1 + 2×1 = 4 — then 4 ÷ 1.414 = 2.828
row 3 writes — 2×2 + 2×2 = 8 — then 8 ÷ 1.414 = 5.657; the bar beside it is longest
the ÷√2 column ghosts terracotta and a caption sets: 'd_k = 2. This step is in the real operation too.'

props.scaleCaption: d_k = 2. This step is in the real operation too.

beats.act: ACT II — step 2: softmax to weights
beats.narration_text: Softmax turns those three scores into three weights that sum to one. Not probabilities of anything — a mixing recipe. Bank keeps zero point seven six eight of itself. River gets zero point one eight seven. The gets forty-five thousandths.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no softmax scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.
beats.honesty_gate: Weights print to 3 d.p. because 2 d.p. would display 0.05 + 0.19 + 0.77 = 1.01. The running total on screen must land on exactly 1.000.

shot.visual_intent: The three scaled scores physically become three shares of one bar. The sum-to-one is shown by a running total that lands on 1.000 — the normalization is demonstrated, not claimed.

show.event: the three scaled scores carry over from B04 in the same row order, positions held
the softmax expression sets once, small, above the rows
each score's bar re-scales into its weight share; a unit bar assembles beneath from the three segments
a caption sets beside the unit bar: 'Sums to 1 by construction. Not a claim about the world.'
bank's segment fills — the largest, terracotta, the ONE accent — and its weight counter rolls to 0.768
river's segment fills; counter rolls to 0.187
'the' segment fills; counter rolls to 0.045; the running total snaps to 1.000 and holds

props.caption: Sums to 1 by construction. Not a claim about the world.

beats.act: ACT III — step 3: the weighted sum, and the vector moves
beats.narration_text: Now spend the weights. Multiply each token's value vector by its weight, and add them up. Bank went in at two, two. It comes out at one point five eight, two point one four. Money down, water up — moved toward river. But look how far it actually moved: zero point four four units. Bank kept most of itself. Attention revised this vector; it did not replace it.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no weighted-sum / vector-displacement scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.
beats.honesty_gate: The arrow shows the ACTUAL computed displacement (0.44 units), not an exaggerated one. Attention revises the vector; it does not teleport it, and the narration says 'moved toward', never 'became'.

shot.visual_intent: The payoff. Left: the three weighted contributions add up in a column, term by term. Right: the same plane from B03, with `bank` visibly leaving (2,2) and stopping at (1.58, 2.14). The arrow is short on purpose — that honesty is the lesson.

beats.act: ACT III — the chapter's sentence, computed
beats.narration_text: Swap one word. River becomes savings, nothing else changes. Same query, same weights — but a different value vector in the mix. Bank lands at two point one four, one point five eight. Mirrored. That is chapter one's sentence, computed.

beats.narration_text: Now the boundary — and this column matters more than the other one. This was one head, one layer, two dimensions, identity matrices, and numbers I chose. It does not show learned projections, or what stacking the block dozens of times does. And it licenses no quantitative claim at all, because nothing here was measured. It shows the shape of the operation. Nothing more.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no establishes/does-not-establish ledger scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.

shot.visual_intent: A two-column ledger: what the toy licenses, and what it does not. The right column is the longer one, and it is drawn that way deliberately. This is the falsifiability beat — the scope is the content, not a disclaimer under it.

show.event: the two column heads draw: ESTABLISHES (left) · DOES NOT ESTABLISH (right)
the left column fills with the single claim the toy supports: the shape of the operation — score, normalize, mix
right row 1 lands: 'that real learned W_Q/W_K/W_V behave like the identity'
right row 2 lands: 'how multi-head attention splits relations across heads'; a small multi-head fan sketches beside it and stays unlabelled
right row 3 lands: 'what repeated layers do to the representation'; a layer stack ghosts in behind it
right row 4 lands in terracotta — 'any quantitative claim: no number here is measured' — the ONE accent
the full ledger holds, both columns readable at once

left: The shape of one attention operation: score every pair, normalize the scores to weights that sum to 1, return a weighted sum of values.
That a token's vector is therefore context-dependent — the same `bank` resolves differently in two sentences.
right: That real learned W_Q / W_K / W_V behave like the identity matrices used here.
How multi-head attention assigns different relations to different heads, in parallel.
What repeated layers do — how a representation changes as the block is stacked.
That any real model's axes are interpretable directions like 'money' or 'water'.
Any quantitative claim at all: no number in this video is measured.

beats.narration_text: So here is the boundary, said plainly. What this single-head two-dimensional example does not establish is how multi-head attention handles dozens of nuanced semantic dimensions simultaneously. One head, two axes, numbers I chose. A real model runs many heads in parallel over far more dimensions than two — and nothing you just watched tells you what any of those heads learn.
beats.gate_l: MISS — no single-head-vs-multi-head scene in the library. New component on Ch1Chrome.
beats.honesty_gate: The right-hand heads are drawn UNLABELLED. Labelling them would claim to explain multi-head attention, which is the one thing this beat exists to say the video has not done.

shot.visual_intent: The brief's boundary sentence, full-frame and verbatim, over a density comparison: the one head and two named axes the viewer actually watched, against a grid of unlabelled heads each stacking many dimensions. The argument is carried by the size difference, not by a caption.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A static embedding gives one vector per token. Attention scores every pair, normalizes those scores into weights, and returns a weighted sum of value vectors. That is why bank after river differs from bank after savings. The toy numbers were constructed. The operation was not.

shot.visual_intent: The Claude artifact page holds the five claims this reel licenses, numbered by the card itself.

show.event: 0.5s lead pause, then the artifact page opens
the card's own numbered line lands as it is spoken
the fifth line holds alone

props.artifactHeading: What this example licenses you to say
artifactLines: A static embedding gives one vector per token, regardless of context.
Attention scores every token pair, then normalizes those scores into weights that sum to 1.
The output is a weighted sum of value vectors — so a token's vector is revised, not replaced.
That is why `bank` after `river` differs from `bank` after `savings`.
The numbers were constructed for legibility. The operation they illustrate was not.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. "Take two sentences that reuse one word in different senses. Build a two-dimensional toy attention example by hand — show the dot products, the softmax weights, and the output vector. Then tell me which part of your toy is a lie." That last clause is the whole assignment. Every toy lies somewhere. Make it say where.
